Likelihood Intervals for Regression Effect Sizes

Source: R/betaLB-lb.R
LB.Rd

Fit covariance-likelihood regions for independently sampled random regressors. Compute requested effects, types and confidence levels in one native batch, then use the effect extractors to select stored results.

Usage

LB(
  object,
  type = c("mvn", "robust"),
  alpha = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001),
  effects = c("beta", "rsq", "scor", "pcor", "deltarsq", "diffbeta", "fsq"),
  std_y = TRUE,
  std_x = TRUE,
  blocks = list(),
  control = list()
)

Arguments

object

Unweighted, full-rank scalar-response lm fit with an intercept, stored model frame, no offsets and positive residual variance.

type

Character vector containing mvn, robust, or both.

alpha

Distinct significance levels in (0, 1).

effects

Requested families: beta, rsq, scor, pcor, deltarsq, diffbeta, and fsq.

std_y

Whether to standardize the response for slope targets.

std_x

Logical flags or names of model-matrix predictors to standardize for slope targets. Other effects keep their definitions.

blocks

Named list of additional predictor blocks, identified by model-matrix column names or indices, for increments and local f-squared.

control

Named list: maxeval is the native evaluation budget per endpoint; tolerance is its normalized verification tolerance.

Value

Context of class lb, containing named point estimates, a long intervals table and per-row endpoint diagnostics. Failed endpoints are NA with a specific status. Extractors return betalb objects. Slope/contrast target IDs retain their standardization flags.

Details

Normal theory uses divisor-n Gaussian covariance likelihood. Robust calibration uses empirical fourth moments. Signed scalar targets use a target-specific variance ratio; multi-coefficient nonnegative effects use conservative vector projection and a largest-eigenvalue robust cutoff. These are asymptotic procedures, without a finite-sample coverage guarantee.

Author

Ivan Jacob Agaloos Pesigan

Examples

fit <- stats::lm(formula = mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
out <- LB(object = fit, type = "mvn", alpha = 0.05, effects = "rsq")
RSqLB(object = out)
#> Call:
#> LB(object = fit, type = "mvn", alpha = 0.05, effects = "rsq")
#> 
#> Likelihood intervals (vector projections are conservative)
#> type = "mvn"
#>   effect type alpha estimate  lower  upper lower_status upper_status
#> 1    rsq  mvn  0.05   0.7528 0.5629 0.8686           ok           ok
#> 2    adj  mvn  0.05   0.7446 0.5483 0.8643           ok           ok
#>      calibration dimension
#> 1 scalar_profile         1
#> 2 scalar_profile         1
